sorrowfully chapter 5 nathaniel and the cosmic womb from the journal of nathaniel rusk july 5 i place my pen to paper this time just like the last unsure where to start what i hope to accomplishindeed thats a mystery even to myself it exists in a cloud a rarefied region far too distant to grasp here i sit with blood in my eyes wishing to dig past my corporeal form and pour my soul upon these pages but my mind is forever traveling faster than my weary hand can scrawl still i do what i can to snatch ideas from the ether to consign them to paper before theyre lost knowing that no eyes but mine own shall ever read this sad memoir anyway life can be grand sometimes those sparkling instants that make me feel as if i can finally peel off this mask i wear to hide my frailties and show the world that im still alive still kicking those moments never last though the things weve done and endured both good and bad never leave us they may retreat into the shadow realms of our subconscious but all it takes is a certain scent or song to bring them rushing back the past never fades completely it bides its time patiently until it can reemerge for maximum discomfort i dream a lot sometimes it seems as if dreams are the only things keeping me earthtethered lead anvils anchoring my hot air balloon soul the deliveryman came today he visits often twice or thrice a week just after lunch i detected a subtle shift in my homes ambiance heralding something amiss i arrived at the peephole in time to see boot heels fleeing the vicinity as always my dread was interwoven with morbid anticipation the package bore no return address as per usual no delivery address either not even a stamp for legitimacy just a nondescript brown box therein i discovered a photograph the snapshot featured an elderly woman her faded hair tied in a loose ponytail her face was old leather her smile nearly a wince on the back of the photo was scrawled henrietta adams delaney park 135 pm ask her about the pigeons i pocketed the picture and discarded the box i sat around the house until the appointed time and then took the bus to delaney park as i claimed my seat my fellow passengers spared me no glances an occurrence ive grown quite accustomed to with an exhaust blast the dingy vehicle hurled itself forward three stops later id arrived albeit three minutes late frantically i whipped my head left to right right to left seeking the woman from the photograph initially i believed the park empty its grassy stretch unmarred by blanket basket or frisbee but there she was fifty feet leftward readying herself for a departure before a splintery bench she stood breadcrumbs scattered at her feet wearing a tattered pink shawl over a yellow sundress not a single bird pecked at those breadcrumbs miss adams i shouted we need to talk closing the intervening distance i noticed a profound suspicion nestled within the wrinklefolds of her face howdo you know my name she asked sit down for a minute and ill tell ya i pleaded motioning to the bench reluctantly the woman complied henrietta i was sent here to speak with you who sent you the government she was growing agitated i knew that i was treading on eggshells i dont rightly know maam a package showed up on my doorstep your photograph was inside of it on the back of that picture your name was written as was the name of this park and the time youd be here why me thats what im hoping to find out im supposed to ask you about the pigeons she relaxed ah yes the pigeons she sighed i used to feed them healthy breadcrumbs but now i give them poison i watch them sicken and perish and its sodelightfully cathartic i noticed a paper bag in her hand and snatched it away within it breadcrumbs reeked of ammonia where are all the pigeons henrietta not one was in sight usually delaney park is full of em filthy creatures that will shit on you if ya dont keep an eye outcomfortable in their elevation knowing you cant retaliate look behind that bush there with one gnarled forefinger she indicated an area roughly twenty feet distant a profusion of oaks and shrubbery trudging to that vicinity i realized that shed been truthful henrietta mustve been a very busy woman for there were dozens of pigeon corpses there piled behind a bush in varied stages of putrefaction glassy eyes stared with no intelligence behind them inert wings had flapped their last flaps coldly i wondered how her bounty had gone undiscovered returning to her i saw that henrietta now had drool spilling down her chin did you see em she asked her eyes glistening with excitement yeah i saw them so what sonothing there is no greater significance none whatsoever they exist to be slaughtered as do all of gods creatures do you wish to die henrietta her lined leathery brow contracted as she pondered that query after a lengthy pause that seemed to span hours she replied sometimes that was all i needed to hear taking the old gal by the hand i escorted her over to her dead bird collection in the shadow of an imposing oak tree she seemed older than time i looked around the park ensuring that we were still alone look at your pigeons one last time henrietta what do you see they are beautiful better in death than in life goodbye henrietta gripping her face i violently twisted it rightward her neck broke with a loud crack but she voiced not an utterance carefully lowering her until her head met the pigeon mound i noticed that henriettas yellow sundress had wrinkled up on itself after carefully smoothing it out i plucked a pigeon from the corpse heap this i settled upon henriettas chest and folded her arms over it the effect was a skosh surreal evocative of a little girl snoozing with her favorite stuffed animal with a sigh i walked back to the bus stop july 7 another morning another package again no postage stamp i brought the thing to my battered deskwhere im currently seated writing this tearing past the cardboard i discovered a wooden frame bordering a picture of yours truly age five sharing that photo space my parents proudly beamed behind my young self as i exhaled upon birthday cake candles i considered the image for a moment adrift in my own history and then shattered the glass on the back of the photo was a message nathaniel your father and i are so proud of you congratulations on your big promotion i found this filibusters proving meaningless and unable to serve as a political variable rather than focusing on restraining the administration the party is expending more energy on internal strife by contrast the democratic party of korea dpk moved on the 22nd to pursue a merger with the rebuilding korea party further expanding its size with the exception of constitutional amendment there is virtually nothing it cannot do as the dpk grows ever larger and the ppp becomes increasingly incapacitated it has become common for major state affairs and political issues to turn into situations where the democratic party of korea is fighting the democratic party of korea on issues such as prosecutorial reform the expulsion of former floor leader kim byunggi foreign and security policy and nuclear power hardliners within the dpkincluding party leader chung cheongraehave frequently voiced positions at odds with president lee around the presidential office complaints are being voiced less about the ppp and more about dpk hardliners who openly challenge the president since legislation to create a public prosecution office and a serious crimes investigation office was unveiled on the 12th dpk hardliners have openly criticized figures close to the president lawmaker kim yongmin raised his voice at justice minister jung sungho during a national assembly session saying that prosecutors influence was far too strong to which the minister responded please dont think of all prosecutors as criminals this clash between a rulingparty judiciary committee member and the justice minister spread widely as shortform videos while progovernment youtube channels poured out accusations that presidential secretary for civil affairs bongwook justice minister jung sungho and prime minister kim minseok had ruined prosecutorial reform even on the 13th when president lee was departing for a koreajapan summit he spoke with dpk leader chung cheongrae at the airport about the prosecution reform plan president lee emphasized the need to maintain checks on the police saying there must be mutual oversight especially when prosecutorial powers are being reduced after the meeting the presidential office conveyed the presidents message that the party should deliberate and the government should gather opinions ordinarily this would have ended the matter followed by behindthescenes coordination between the president and the ruling party however chung appeared on a progovernment youtube channel and framed the episode as an airport reversal portraying the governments decision to revise its proposal as his own achievement in reality it is common sense that the governments proposal reflects the presidents intent yet the ruling party leader voiced a different position saying that the bill could be revised as much as necessary in the national assembly president lees remark to chung at a dinner with dpk leadersasking are you perhaps antileeis difficult to dismiss as a mere joke one attendee reportedly said that about 5 percent of it was sincere ultimately at a press conference on the 21st president lee issued what amounted to an ultimatum to dpk hardliners opposing supplementary investigative powers stating that there are exceptional cases where supplementary investigative authority for prosecutors is necessary the planned merger with the rebuilding korea partywhich had criticized the prosecution reform plan even more harshly than dpk hardlinerscould become yet another variable the conflict between dpk leader chung cheongrae and former floor leader kim byunggi which has continued since last year came to a temporary close with kims expulsion from the party however allegations that kim tacitly condoned bribery in candidate nominations ignored a petition involving 30 million won granted preferential employment to his child and misused corporate credit cards through his wife were raised not by the opposition ppp but by insiders such as aides within the dpk this has fueled analysis that kims sudden exitafter leading nonlee faction purges in nominations and becoming floor leader in the first year of the lee jaemyung administrationwas the result of internal power struggles chung led the push to expel kim kims successor han byungdo is considered prolee but shares activistgeneration ties with chung in the byelections for the dpk supreme council several figures aligned with chung including moon jungbok and lee sungyoon were elected consolidating a chung cheongrae onetop leadership structure chung is again pushing for a one person one vote system for delegates and rankandfile members a proposal that failed last december due to resistance from prolee factions prolee figures view this as a move to secure chungs reelection at the party convention scheduled for august prime minister kim minseok is currently mentioned as a potential rival dpk hardliners are now closely watching issues of foreign policy security and nuclear energy contrary to expectations since taking office president lee has not significantly departed from the previous administrations stance on the uskorea alliance or trilateral cooperation among south korea the united states and japan on nuclear power although he initially appointed antinuclear figures to the presidential office and cabinet he has recently opted for realism including approving new nuclear plant construction a dpk official said however for now they are watching but if the president continues to adhere to a us and japancentered diplomatic line and current nuclear policy a conflict between the president and the ruling party will eventually erupt this suggests that clashes or mutual checks between a presidentcentered dpk and a hardlinercentered opposition dpk could continue into the administrations second year the ruling dpks confidence in occasionally playing the role of the oppositioneven against its own presidentstems from its belief that internal factional conflict remains manageable if this pattern continues voters may come to perceive an extension of dpk rule as a change of government from one democratic party of korea to another some observers even predict that korean politics could shift away from a traditional twoparty system toward a oneandahalfparty system in which the dpk competes against a collection of nondpk parties similar to japans longdominant liberal democratic party professor kang wontaek of seoul national university said the conflict between the democratic party of korea and the president can be seen as internal strife but it may also signal a move toward a predominant party system in which one party simultaneously plays the roles of ruling party and opposition indeed since 2016 the dpk has won three consecutive general elections two presidential elections and split one local election win and one loss although the ppp won the 2022 presidential election the margin was only 07 percentage points meaning the dpks overall record can be viewed as six wins one draw and one loss out of eight contests as legislative power continues to grow the dpk scored consecutive landslide victories in the 2020 and 2024 general elections demographic and regional trendssuch as overwhelming support among voters aged 40 and over and strength in the seoul metropolitan areasuggest that the dpks dominance is structurally likely to continue for the time being professor kang added for a oneparty system to solidify either the opposing party must collapse or the dominant party must constantly innovate britains conservative party expanded its base among the working class and centrists through ideological flexibility and overcame crises with bold generational change under leaders like david cameron japans liberal democratic party likewise broadened its support through decisive welfare and labor reforms with former prime minister junichiro koizumi famously declaring that he would destroy the ldp to drive change in korea however both the 2020 and 2024 general elections were decided less by dpk innovation than by the selfdestruction of its rival despite various controversies the national barometer survey nbs released on the 22nd showed president lees approval rating at 59 down just 2 percentage points party support stood at 40 for the dpk and 20 for the ppp

event the guardians of democracy 11 february 2026 braslia supremo tribunal federal the meeting did not receive a title fit for history it was filed as coordinationan internal session among ministers and senior clerks slotted between hearings and dispatches one more entry in a calendar that had grown dense since 8 january 2023 turned the court into both tribunal and target there would be no press note no photograph at the doorway no preemptive framing the stf had learned the hard way that announcements do not inform they invite interpretation they did not gather to relitigate the past though the past sat in the room like an additional participant the court had already sentenced and processed hundreds connected to the postelection violence and it spoke of that record with the language of duty rather than triumph still the ministers understood that conviction counts and prison terms were not the end of the story they were proof that the state could punish they were not proof that the state could deter the discussion opened as it often did in braslia with the real problem time elections compress institutions they reduce tolerance for procedural delay and enlarge the political cost of every day without an answer in 2026 the court faced a familiar pattern returning in a more modern shapenetworks that had once treated electoral defeat as illegitimate were again building a parallel narrative infrastructure migrating between platforms disguising coordination as spontaneity refining messages for speed and saturation a clerk summarized recent intelligence and technical assessments in language carefully scrubbed of drama synthetic audio was easier to produce and harder to trace altered video no longer required expensive teams coordinated campaigns could be launched faster than courts could respond the tse had already moved to regulate parts of this environment imposing restrictions and disclosure rules on aidriven electoral content the point was not whether those rules were perfect the point was what their existence implied the next electoral cycle would be fought not only at the ballot box but in the informational corridor leading to it then came the subject no one needed to name loudly the inqurito das fake news old enough to feel permanent and controversial enough to be radioactive remained alive outside the court critics spoke of exceptionalism dressed as necessity inside the inquiry was described in operational terms an imperfect perimeter legally defensible by precedent and continuity functionally useful because the political branches had failed to produce coherent tools of their own when ministers spoke about it they did not speak like rulers defending power they spoke like administrators defending a scaffolding they believed the building still required that in turn dragged the tension into the open the accusation that the stf had begun to govern no one in the room treated that charge as pure malice some ministers dismissed it as propaganda others conceded it had roots in reality if only because the courts footprint had expanded into arenas once managed by congress and the executive the debate therefore was not whether the stf should stay out of politicsthat phrase had become meaningless in a year where any decision would be read as partisan regardless of intent the debate was whether restraint under the present conditions was still neutralityor whether it had become a form of abdication a moment of structure emerged in the way structure often emerges at the stf not by vote on a single case but by shared posture the ministers converged on a working assumption for the year procedural permissiveness now carried strategic cost injunctions would need to be faster decisions in matters framed as systemic attacks on democratic order would be interpreted through broader consequences not only narrow disputes coordination with electoral authorities would be treated as routine rather than exceptional whenever disputes threatened to spill into generalized doubt no one called it stricter they called it prevention they called it foresight they called it refusing to be surprised twice in the middle of this alexandre de moraes spoke with the controlled cadence he had adopted over years of becoming both judge and symbol he described what the court faced not as opinion but as organized manipulationnetworks designed to degrade confidence until the state could not function without coercion if the state delayed he argued the delay would be interpreted not as fairness but as weakness and weakness in that environment was fuel others pressed from the opposite side they did not dispute the threat they worried about legitimacy if the court moved too expansively it risked deepening the distrust it sought to contain if it moved too narrowly it risked enabling a repeat of institutional collapse the dilemma was not theoretical it was practical and immediate whatever they did would be experienced politically and whatever they failed to do would be exploited politically the court could not escape interpretation it could only choose which consequences it preferred the most revealing part of the meeting was not the rhetoric but the mutual understanding beneath it no one believed the political branches would assume the burden in time congress would posture and bargain the executive would invoke independence when convenient and complain when harmed governors would demand federal force after declaring crises local in that landscape the stf saw itselfuncomfortably even resentfullyas the only institution capable of issuing answers that were final in form even if contested in spirit when the session ended nothing was announced there was no new doctrine no press release no single line crossed that journalists could quote the court returned to its chambers with its posture unchanged in public and sharpened in private the conclusion was simple and to them unavoidable in 2026 the stf would err on the side of interventionprocedural legalistic always described as narrowbecause it had come to believe that neutrality in that particular year would be indistinguishable from surrender and the ministers carried out with them the doubt that never appears in rulings whether tightening their grip would preserve the republics legitimacy or merely confirm to a growing share of the country that legitimacy had already migrated into the hands of those willing to enforce it they did not yet grasp the scale of what they were setting in motionthat a posture agreed in silence filed as routine would radiate outward and leave marks on the country that would outlast the cases the election and perhaps even the republics own pretenses
